current_evidence: Story versions: complete pipeline (1,498 texts; TF-IDF and MiniLM graphs; Louvain x3 seeds; 1,000 label shuffles; degree-preserving null). Traditions: Berezkin matrices 926 x 2,138 (~2016) and 958 x 2,564 (Apr-Oct 2019, CC0 package) inspected
usable_sample: 1,133 joint-cohort versions (164 types); 866 traditions with >= 10 motifs
main_gap: Tradition matrices are 6-9 years behind the catalogue (3,328 motifs / 1,031 traditions in Dec 2025) and dominated by documentation intensity (1-426 motifs per tradition)
verdict: Feasible now (story versions, done); feasible with specified work (tradition level)
smallest_viable_scope: Keep the existing story-version communities; tradition-level communities optional

current_evidence: Existing distance analysis on 1,084 versions (rho -0.063 TF-IDF, -0.110 embeddings, beyond whole-location shuffles); Berezkin centroids for 926 traditions
main_gap: Location means collector attribution (versions) or area centroid (traditions), never origin; collection intensity, language family and 71% European skew compete as explanations
smallest_viable_scope: Existing analysis with explicit location meaning; no origin or route claims

current_evidence: SCCS2002 (all 186 coded), Pulotu (137 Austronesian cultures), DRH (1,687 entries). 190 traditions with any candidate link; 68 rule-validated SCCS identity links; hand review validated 7 of 14 world-religion-coded links
usable_sample: ~21 world-religion-coded traditions (9 Christian, 9 Islam, 3 Buddhist, 0 Hindu) + 37 indigenous after the rule screen; about half expected to survive hand review
main_gap: Tiny sample; religion almost perfectly regional (4 different-religion pairs within 1,500 km); undated motif aggregates vs focal-year codes; codes measure depth of Islamization/Christianization from a mourning-practice study; two incompatible catalogue snapshots
smallest_viable_scope: Descriptive table/map of matched traditions with coverage shown; no association test

current_evidence: SCCS distinguishes only Buddhist branches; DRH has Catholic/Orthodox/Protestant/Sunni/Shi'a tags on religious-group entries, rarely on culture entries (eHRAF-derived: 3/6/0/6/2); Pulotu none
main_gap: No source links Christian or Islamic branches to folklore traditions or story versions; shared scriptures give no branch-specific text corpus

current_evidence: Flood case: ETCSL Sumerian Flood story (fragmentary, (c) ETCSL) and Genesis 6-9 (WEB, public domain); DRH dates Gilgamesh -1900..-130 and Atra-Hasis -1700..-600; Yale lecture: Genesis adapts older Mesopotamian traditions and adds a moral rationale
main_gap: Genesis dating and specific contact not verified here; the earlier narrative is itself religious; text similarity no higher than a same-translation control (embedding 0.511 vs 0.498)
smallest_viable_scope: One evidence-graded case study with primary scholarship cited

component: Religious narrative to later local folklore
current_evidence: Barlaam and Ioasaph apologue (king's son told women are 'Devils that deceive men') found in Gutenberg #749; three later ATU 1678 versions in the corpus (Boccaccio 1350-55, Poggio 15th c., Geiler c. 1510); DRH dates the legend's dissemination 750-1700
main_gap: No inspected scholarly source documents this specific link; Pulotu conversion data have no dated folklore to compare; similarity cannot detect the link (control exemplum scores higher by embedding)
smallest_viable_scope: One evidence-graded candidate case, clearly labelled

current_evidence: Aesop for Children: 144 fables with separable printed morals (PD); Jataka: 547 stories, 533 with editor keywords (ABT revision, no licence found; Cowell original PD); 7 Gospel parables segmented (WEB, PD); corpus: 34 versions state a lesson; 29 tale types with 36 religious-collection and 257 other versions. Pilot: 30 stories segmented; TF-IDF ranked all 6 pre-declared plot parallels 1st or 2nd
usable_sample: 117-version annotation frame (all 36 religious-collection versions + up to 3 others per type) in 29 types
main_gap: No outcome/lesson labels exist; lessons are mostly unstated (16 of the 293 frame versions state one); printed morals are edition-specific; framing must be hand-coded (2 of 3 regex 'scripture' hits were false)
smallest_viable_scope: Codebook + double coding of ~50 and single coding of the rest; within-type comparison across framings with a shuffle baseline

current_evidence: Corpus has edition/publication years (85% of versions; median earliest 1888) and scrape dates; Berezkin is an undated aggregate (M&X give first/mean publication year per tradition); Pulotu time foci; DRH dated religious entries
